redFirst.basis: `node --test tests/evals.test.mjs` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1, but its output carries no test tally this command reads, so an assertion failure cannot be told from a crash - no test is known to have been collected: no tally or error reader matched its output, so no line of it is quoted as decisive; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD; no ignored dependency directory linked from the project root; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home); deadline: 480s, the default - the command is not a sweep naming suites, so there is no recorded cost to size it from

outcome.technical: Added skills/architecture-map/evals/evals.json (5 evals, skill-creator format; checkable statements are in the field `expectations`, which is skill-creator's schema name for what the task calls assertions; each eval has 7-8), skills/architecture-map/evals/README.md (env vars ARCHMAP_EVAL_REPO_A/B/C, workspace .claude/archmap/evals/ under the home directory, with-skill vs without-skill, generate_review.py, balanced vs max on eval 1), and tests/evals.test.mjs (e1-e5). Prompts reference only the env vars (A for evals 1-3, B for 4, C for 5), carry no machine path; .private checklists and ground truth are referenced as .private/reference/<file> relative to the archmap checkout. Full `node --test` run: 273 pass, 0 fail (denylist test d1 included). I also grepped the new files against every term of .private/anonymise-denylist.txt (no term printed): no hits, which matters because the new files were untracked and d1 reads only git ls-files. Dependants: README.md and the tests listed are unaffected because nothing references the new files by path; the two paths .private/reference/eval-{a,b,c}-*.md named in expectations do not exist yet and are for the owner to create, as the brief says ground truth stays private. The files evals.json/README.md/evals.test.mjs were last declared by blocked tasks P8.3/P8.4/P8.6; I did not touch those tasks.
outcome.descriptive: The skill-creator eval set (5 evals) and its runbook now exist with no repo location or client name in tracked files, locked by a 5-case test.

testsAdded: tests/evals.test.mjs: evals.json parses with exactly five evals ids 1-5 each with prompt, expected_output and at least three assertions; prompts carry no absolute or home-relative path and reference only ARCHMAP_EVAL_REPO_A/B/C (mapping A,A,A,B,C); no machine path and .private referenced only relative; README names the three env vars, workspace directory, generate_review.py, without-skill; the path detector itself is proven on good and bad samples
